newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW-Nail sees lengthy talks on GFSA.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Nail sees lengthy talks on GFSA.

text.p: Negotiations for New Africa Investment Ltd (Nail) to take control of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd with Rembrandt Group Ltd are likely to be lengthy, Nail's deputy chairman said on Thursday.
"Obviously we want it to be concluded as soon as possible, but these things tend to take some time...We could be talking about quite a while," Cyril Ramaphosa told Reuters.
"The aim is to enter into a partnership with Rembrandt in the control of Gold Fields...(but) discussions are still at a very preliminary stage."
Nail aims to buy an effective 17.2 percent stake in the mining group, giving it joint control of the world's third largest gold producer with Rembrandt which already owns a similar stake.
Ramaphosa said various possibilities were being investigated in terms of funding the acquisition, which would cost over 1.8 billion rand at current market prices.
But the parties to the deal had not yet got down to a detailed discussion of price, he said.
"The discussions on price have not yet really started. We are still very much at a formative or preliminary stage."
Shares in Gold Fields rose 9.25 to 119.00 rand on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange following the announcement of the planned bid.
But several analysts doubted any significant premium would be involved in the deal given that Nail was the only bidder in the frame.
"I doubt there'll be a premium paid. They're the only onds bidding and its looking like just a simple transference of shares," said Nick Goodwin, mining analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.

Ramaphosa declined to detail his plans for the diversified mining group, but said the move by black business to acquire a new mining stake was part of a clear pattern of growing black economic empowerment.

"Black businesses are surging forward. Black businesses' share on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange is increasing on an ongoing basis and I think soon we are going to have a fairly sizeable representation of black business in terms of listed companies."
Ramaphosa, a former secretary-general of the African National Congress and one-time leader of the National Union Mineworkers, is seen as the driving force behind the Gold Fields deal.
Nail already has control of industrial group Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd, but it lost out earlier this year in the fight to win South Africa's sixth biggest mining house JCI Ltd.
That deal was finally clinched by another black empowerment consortium, African Mining Group, led by Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd.

Nail hopes to acquire from Gold Fields and its Driefontein Consolidated Ltd unit their 40 percent shareholding in Asteroid Ltd. Asteroid holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings Ltd which, in turn, holds 43 percent of Gold Fields.
Rembrandt already holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings. The addition of a similar holding by Nail would give the two partners 34.4 percent control of Gold Fields.
